Floor 23 -> 12: pointer-to-volatile defeats cse dest-recording (cse.c:7329), condition-before-read fills the load-delay slots, three pointer locals reproduce target's three lui/addiu bases — build is

Permuter axis measured DEAD: 50,425 iterations across two structurally different chassis never beat the honest floor of 18, the permuter's own metric is uncorrelated with the sandbox here, its single

Directed-permuter axis KILLED: 1,008 forms enumerated exhaustively and sandbox-scored across two cross-products (plus 1,152 permuter iterations over the same spaces), best 18 in both waves; three of t

First cc1 -da dump of the floor-18 form itself: the 'combine folds %lo' model and the 'v0/v1 swap is a steerable RA tie' model are both REFUTED from the RTL, seven live-range-surgery forms measured de

Forensics: the target's exact flag-section signature (lbu 5 / sb 5 / lui 4, three addend-0 bases, four surviving reloads) is reachable in NON-VOLATILE C via a cse basic-block boundary — refuting the s

Rederive: 16 structurally new shapes measured; found a SECOND, zero-cost, non-volatile cse mechanism that produces all four target reloads (invalidate_skipped_block), proved it incompatible with the t

frontier.hypothesis: Every construct that ends the cse basic block between two flag blocks costs at least one instruction the target does not contain, or is a forbidden no-semantic-purpose construct - and the only zero-cost reload mechanism (AROUND / invalidate_skipped_block) is incompatible with the target's unconditional store. If that holds, this is the escalation thesis and the F3 packet should be rewritten around it.
frontier.mechanism: cse_end_of_basic_block's extension (cse.c:8102-8184) declines only on LABEL_NUSES != 1, a CODE_LABEL inside the arm, or a used CODE_LABEL immediately preceding the join label; s8 showed each of the three requires an extra jump insn or a dead-goto label pad. The claim that remains unproven is completeness: that no OTHER C construct reaches those three states.
frontier.next_probe: Do NOT file from a non-escalation modality. The two remaining honest lines of attack before it becomes an escalation: (1) enumerate what else creates a CODE_LABEL in GCC 2.7.2's RTL stream that C can reach without a jump - switch/ADDR_VEC labels, computed goto, the loop-exit label of a real loop whose body the target already contains, and the labels emitted by expand_* for && / || short-circuits (an '&&' condition emits TWO conditional branches to ONE false-label, i.e. LABEL_NUSES 2, at the cost of one extra branch - measure whether the boundary it buys is worth more than the branch it costs, which s8 never measured); (2) check whether jump.c's thread_jumps (run before cse1) can be made to redirect a second branch onto an existing join label, raising its NUSES to 2 without a new insn.

frontier.hypothesis: The '&&'-condition boundary pays for itself: 'if ((p[8] & K) && something)' emits two conditional branches to a shared false-label (LABEL_NUSES 2), which ends the cse block at the join and should recover one reload plus one addend-0 base per block (worth ~3 insns) against a 1-insn branch cost.
frontier.mechanism: expand_expr for TRUTH_ANDIF_EXPR emits jumpifnot on each operand to the same label, so the join label of the whole if has two LABEL_REFs and the cse extension at cse.c:8112 declines. It is the ONLY way found so far to raise LABEL_NUSES without an unconditional jump that jump.c will delete.
frontier.next_probe: The honest problem is finding a SECOND condition that is semantically real (the target has no second branch, so any construct here changes the emitted control flow and will show up as an inserted branch in the score). Measure it anyway to put a number on the trade: 'if ((p[8] & K) && p[8])' and similar, honest-scored, plus a cse.fn check that the boundary actually materialises. If the boundary is confirmed to produce the target's per-block signature, the finding is that the SIGNATURE is buyable and only the branch is in the way - which is the strongest possible exhibit for the escalation packet.

frontier.hypothesis: The one-object re-derivation (0x80106A70..73 as a single declared u8[4], flag byte = element 3) is not measurable in the sandbox even if it is correct, because engine/score.py does not mask NAMED-symbol relocation addends.
frontier.mechanism: score.py masks section-relative HI16/LO16 addends only ([[sandbox-lo16-text-addend-false-distance]]); a build spelling the flag byte as &D_80106A70[3] emits R_MIPS_HI16/LO16 against D_80106A70 with addend 3 where the reference object has D_80106A73 with addend 0. The two link to the SAME bytes (both symbols are absolute addresses in undefined_syms_auto.txt), so the sandbox would report a false non-zero distance for a byte-correct form. s2's original kill of this hypothesis cited relocations that a shipped PS-EXE does not have, and s3 already voided that premise.
frontier.next_probe: Requires touching include/code6cac.h:462 (the extern u8 D_80106A70 declaration), which is outside a grind session's single-file scope and would change other functions' codegen - so it needs an owner decision, not a probe. Before spending anything on it, note that the array model does NOT solve the boundary problem (cse still merges the address pseudos), so it can only ever explain the addressing, never the reloads.
